definition: An LLM that consumes and/or produces audio tokens natively, unifying ASR, TTS, and spoken dialogue in one model.
details: An LLM that consumes and/or produces audio tokens natively, unifying ASR, TTS, and spoken dialogue in one model. Enables paralinguistic understanding (tone, emotion, hesitation) that cascaded ASR-then-text pipelines discard.

explainer.lead: An LLM that consumes and/or produces audio tokens natively, unifying ASR, TTS, and spoken dialogue in one model. It matters because it enables paralinguistic understanding of tone, emotion, and hesitation that cascaded pipelines discard.

tiers.eli5: Instead of turning speech into text, answering, then turning text back into speech, one model listens and speaks directly.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use a single model for recognition, synthesis, and dialogue, gaining access to tone and hesitation cues. A pitfall is that cascaded ASR-then-text pipelines throw away exactly those paralinguistic signals.
tiers.paperLevel: A speech LLM natively consumes and/or produces audio tokens, unifying ASR, TTS, and spoken dialogue in one model. Limit: the description covers native audio handling, not text-only behaviour.

explainer.example: A spoken dialogue system uses one speech LLM to hear the user's tone of hesitation and reply in speech within the same model.
